comparisons.peer_topic: Net Charge-Offs and Provision for Credit Losses Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Net charge-offs for 2024 were $6.0 billion, up from $3.8 billion in 2023, primarily due to credit card loans and the commercial real estate office portfolio. The provision for credit losses increased $1.4 billion to $5.8 billion, driven by credit card and small business loan growth and asset quality deterioration in commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC reported increases in net credit losses driven largely by credit card portfolios and macroeconomic factors, though C experienced a larger percentage increase (45%) and specific vintage maturation impacts, while BAC saw net charge-offs rise from $3.8 billion to $6.0 billion due to credit card loans and commercial real estate office portfolios. C's net credit losses were $7.6 billion with lower FICO customers primarily driving the increase, whereas BAC did not specify FICO bands but highlighted the rise in credit card losses as a primary driver alongside commercial real estate.
